title: When You Have Eaten and Are Full

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: I learned Your name where nothing grew,
On bread that fell like morning dew.
You let me hunger, let me see
The stranger living inside me.
My coat held out, my feet stayed sound,
Forty years of holy ground.

sections.label: Pre-Chorus
lines: The desert never was the test.
The danger is the day I'm blessed.

sections.label: Chorus
lines: When I have eaten and am full,
Let me bless You for the land.
When the table's long and the barns are tall,
Let me still see Your hand.
Oh, beware, my soul, beware,
Do not forget.
Do not forget.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Now water rises from the hills,
The vine, the fig, the field that fills.
I built a house, I latched the door,
I counted, and I wanted more.
And somewhere in the gold and grain,
My heart began to praise my name.

sections.label: Pre-Chorus
lines: It's said so softly no one hears:
"My hand, my might, my working years."

sections.label: Chorus
lines: When I have eaten and am full,
Let me bless You for the land.
When the table's long and the barns are tall,
Let me still see Your hand.
Oh, beware, my soul, beware,
Do not forget.
Do not forget.

sections.label: Bridge
lines: Who led me past the serpent's sting?
Who split the flint and made it spring?
Who fed me bread my fathers never knew?
The strength to gather came from You.
The hand that earns was given, too.

sections.label: Final Chorus
lines: When I have eaten and am full,
Let me bless You for the land.
When the table's long and the barns are tall,
Let me still see Your hand.
Oh, beware, my soul, beware,
Do not forget.
(Do not forget.)

sections.label: Outro
lines: Not by bread alone,
But by every word.
When I am full,
Remember.

epigraph: When thou hast eaten and art full, then thou shalt bless the LORD thy God for the good land which he hath given thee
